title: The break count has no field and the break limit has no governed row, so the element of a broken plan has no published identifier
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-011 Data table; TC-E3-011-02, TC-E3-011-03); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.11.1 to A2.11.4.4, R-RES-29, R-RES-30, BR-S2-011); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T3.1, T3.2, T8, T-A.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31, R-RES-36); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md (treatment, recovery_case, rule_row); _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 6 and 7; s7 Target reading; s8 BR2, BR3; s11 Data; s12.5; s13 Database; CON s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1, AC3; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.5, s13
description: Both break criteria turn on two numbers, the count of breaks the case has carried and the limit it is tested against, and neither has a home in the target. The legacy Data table names recovery_case, v_ace_payment, treatment, decision_log_entry and rule_row with their field ranges and no break count; TSD S2 T3.1 gives treatment DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 with no break_count, no max_breaks and no plan-state column, and the Logical Data Model has no DF-TRT row for either; recovery_case carries DF-CAS-046 plan_ref, DF-CAS-047 plan_status and DF-CAS-048 plan_status_as_of, which are the ACE plan status as read and not a count; the routing logic states the conditions as break_count < max_breaks and break_count >= max_breaks with no governed row identifier for either value, and the only value in the sources is restructure.max_breaks = 2 in the Temporal and Drools Design example, which is a parameter name and not a row. The stories therefore compose the count per calculation from the case's own treatment rows whose outcome is BROKEN (DF-TRT-013, LOV-TRT-OUTCOME) and the count the case signal carries, take the limit from the rule row in force and write both into the PlanBreak element with the rule version, and they declare no break-count column in rwb_treatment.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E3-011 Data table: recovery_case (17 more fields), v_ace_payment (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054), treatment (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014), decision_log_entry (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018), rule_row (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015); no break count. TSD S2 T3.1: treatment fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033, no break_count and no max_breaks; T3.2 lists LOV-TRT-OUTCOME KEPT, BROKEN, COMPLETED, CANCELED, DECLINED with no count list. Logical Data Model v8: treatment row of 21 fields with no break count; recovery_case DF-CAS-046 to DF-CAS-048 are plan_ref, plan_status, plan_status_as_of. Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-RES-36 use break_count and max_breaks as terms with no reference-data row. Context pack S2 ownership rows: one table (treatment), four REST operations, one event, no job, one workflow.
area: Data model and reference data, S2 rwb-treatment with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect of S2 with the data owner of the Logical Data Model and the owner of the rwb-decision rule registry
proposed: Allocate DF-TRT identifiers for the break count and the limit if they are to be persisted, or confirm the composition rule in the Logical Data Model; publish max_breaks as a governed row of rwb-decision with an identifier and a version, and name the row in R-RES-30 and R-RES-31 as the routing logic names the condition.

title: REQ-S2-009 says a broken plan raises an event, and the ownership rows and the plan give this legacy key no event to raise
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (Requirements served, REQ-S2-009); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4.md (EV-10, EV-11, EV-12); _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows: one event, EV-10); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T5.3, T8); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-09, R5.7)
section: APP s7 AC1; s12.3, s12.4, s12.9; s19; CON s2 Business rationale; s7 AC4; s12.3; s19
description: REQ-S2-009 states the outcome this feature serves as 'a broken plan raises an event and returns the case to a decision rather than leaving it in a plan state'. The plan gives the two stories of this legacy key no DP-09 dependency (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), the ownership rows of S2 name exactly one event, EV-10 TreatmentApproved, and the event catalogue carries EV-10, EV-11 TreatmentBooked and EV-12 PaymentMissed with no plan-broken event and no rwb.treatment.PlanBroken.v1 name. The two stories therefore deliver the 'event' as the BREAK_RECORDED stage report the break branch sends to the parent CaseWorkflow as a Temporal signal inside the case, publish no Kafka event and write no outbox row, and the contract records the refusal and the gap. A Kafka event would be a new subscription and a new outbox path on the event platform, which is platform work of DP-09 and not this legacy key.
evidence: FSD S2 requirements table: REQ-S2-009 with no event name and no consumer; TSD S2 T5.3 lists TreatmentApproved as the only event of the module; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-10 to EV-12 carry treatmentId, terms, bookingRef and businessDate, dueDate and amountDue, and no plan-broken event; context pack S2 ownership rows give one event, EV-10; the split plan rows of RWB-S2-E3011-APP and RWB-S2-E3011-CON carry H RWB-S2-E3011-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON only.
area: Events and integration, S2 rwb-treatment with P7 rwb-decision and P9 rwb-reporting
owner_role: Solution architect with the owner of the Kafka event platform and the business analyst of module S2
proposed: Either confirm the stage report to rwb-case as the event REQ-S2-009 means and reword the requirement, or allocate the event, its name rwb.treatment.PlanBroken.v1, its payload and its consumers, add DP-09 with H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON to both stories and add the outbox row, then fold it into the wave 2 event catalogue.

title: No source says where the plan status of a broken plan is held after the split, and the ACE plan view is read only
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md (recovery_case DF-CAS-046 to DF-CAS-048, LOV-PLAN-STATUS, v_ace_plan DF-ACE-160 to DF-ACE-177); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T3.1 DF-TRT-013, DF-TRT-014, T3.2 LOV-TRT-OUTCOME); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31, R-RES-36); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.11.3.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-011 Screen and states)
section: APP s4 Flow steps 7 and 8; s7 Target reading; s8 BR7; s9; s11 Data; s12.7; CON s7 AC1, AC4; s12.1, s12.7
description: A broken plan is a state of the case (PLAN_BROKEN, then BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION or RESTRUCTURE_BARRED) and a state of the treatment (outcome BROKEN), and three places can hold it: recovery_case.plan_status with LOV-PLAN-STATUS 'created, approved, booked or broken' and plan_status_as_of, which the Logical Data Model sources from ACE; treatment.outcome with LOV-TRT-OUTCOME and outcome_at, which TSD S2 gives to this module; and the ACE plan itself through v_ace_plan, which is read only. No source says which of them the break step writes and which follows from the case rule, and the legacy screen shows one state list, 'Draft; submitted; approved; booked; broken', for the treatment record. The stories write the treatment mark and the element here and leave every case status to rwb-case, which applies the rule and keeps recovery_case.plan_status; the contract states that boundary and no story writes a case row.
evidence: Logical Data Model v8: recovery_case plan_ref varchar(30), plan_status varchar(10) LOV-PLAN-STATUS, plan_status_as_of date, all sourced from ACE; v_ace_plan read-only with DF-ACE-160 to DF-ACE-177 including plan_status and closed_reason. TSD S2 T3.1: treatment outcome varchar(12) LOV-TRT-OUTCOME, outcome_at timestamptz; T3.2 LOV-TRT-OUTCOME KEPT, BROKEN, COMPLETED, CANCELED, DECLINED. Routing logic: the to states are case states. Legacy RWB-E3-011 screen table: SCR-14 with the five states.
area: State model and data ownership, S2 rwb-treatment with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect with the owner of P3 rwb-case and the data owner of the Logical Data Model
proposed: Confirm that the treatment outcome is this service's mark and that recovery_case.plan_status follows the case rule applied by rwb-case, and say in the Logical Data Model which of the two is authoritative when they disagree after a replay or a late ACE load.

title: The payment window, the columns that decide 'no payment matched' and the cure-period set are unpublished
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.11.3.1 VR-S2-011-1, R-RES-29); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-RES-27, R-RES-28, R-RES-29); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T3.1, T-A.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-011 Data table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 5; s8 BR4, BR5, BR8; s11 Data; s12.5, s12.8; CON s3 Preconditions; s7 AC2; s12.5
description: R-RES-29 decides the break on the condition 'no payment and cure_period passed' and R-RES-27 starts the cure period with 'cure_period_days from reference data', and no read source publishes the window, the column that decides a match, or the governed row that holds the days. The legacy Data table names v_ace_payment with payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount and 6 more and no match rule; FSD A2.11 states the condition in words and names no column and no days value; TSD S2 T3.1 gives the plan terms of the treatment but no due-date derivation and no payment match; the routing logic names cure_period_days with no set identifier; the Temporal and Drools example gives 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE as an illustration. The stories read the payments at the ACE batch date, test them over the cure window of the plan and read the days from the governed set in force, and they assert no window length and no match column as a value.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.11.3.1: VR-S2-011-1 names v_ace_batch_status only; R-RES-29 condition 'no payment and cure_period passed' with no column and no window; R-RES-30 timer '5 working days'. Routing logic R-RES-27: timer column 'cure_period_days from reference data'. Logical Data Model DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054: payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount and 6 more, no match flag. TSD S2 T-A.1: API-S2-002 read only; no payment operation of this service.
area: Reference data and ACE views, S2 rwb-treatment with P3 rwb-case and ACE
owner_role: Owner of the P3 rwb-case parameters and reference data with ACE and its DBA and the business analyst of module S2
proposed: Publish cure_period_days as a governed reference row with an identifier and a version, name the payment columns and the tolerance that decide a match in the plan terms, and confirm the window as the plan's own cure window rather than a second setting.
